questions.title: Mitosis exclusively produces two identical daughter cells
questions.subject: fnd
questions.question: Both mitosis and meiosis are forms of cell division. Which of the following occurs exclusively in mitotic division?

options.C: Four cells with differing genetic material

explanations.A: Incorrect. Two rounds of division (meiosis I and meiosis II) is a feature specific to meiosis, not mitosis, which involves a single division.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Recombination (crossing-over) is specific to meiosis I's prophase, made possible by homologous chromosome pairing, a step that has no equivalent in mitosis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Four genetically distinct cells is the meiotic outcome, produced by two successive divisions with recombination and independent assortment; this does not occur in mitosis.
explanations.D: Correct. Mitosis, uniquely among the two division types, produces exactly two daughter cells that are genetically identical to each other and to the parent cell, because it involves a single division with no crossing-over or independent assortment of homologues. Meiosis, by contrast, involves two successive divisions and, through crossing-over and independent assortment, produces four genetically distinct haploid cells.

questions.learning_objective: State that mitosis produces two genetically identical, diploid daughter cells from one diploid parent cell, and contrast this with meiosis, which produces four genetically distinct haploid cells.
